title: Mark a grid square and a six-figure grid reference on a topographic map with two markers
instruction: Put the red marker in grid square 3234 and the blue marker on grid reference 346 332.
context: A grid reference gives the easting (read along the bottom or top edge) before the northing (read up the side): "along the corridor, then up the stairs". A four-figure reference names the square whose south-west corner is where its two lines cross, and a six-figure one adds tenths of a square, estimated by eye. Walkers report their position this way and rescue teams plot it; route cards, Scouts and school geography use the same rule. A plot with the numbers swapped or the square read from the wrong corner sends people to the wrong hillside.
setup: Left and right are the robot's. Positions are in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left; heights above the table top. Map board (fixed, taped down): a printed map, laminated in matte film and mounted on 3 mm hardboard, 52 cm along x by 58 cm along y, spanning x 5 to 57 and y -29 to +29. The map is an invented 1:10,000 sheet with north toward the far side: pale terrain (woods, a lake and stream, brown contours round a hill, a road, a track, three buildings), no place names. Its 1 km grid squares are 10 cm on the map, in 4 columns and 3 rows, drawn as dark blue lines 4 mm wide: easting lines 31, 32, 33, 34 and 35 run west to east (east is the robot's right) at y +20, +10, 0, -10 and -20; northing lines 32, 33, 34 and 35 run south to north at x 16, 26, 36 and 46. The printed face spans x 13 to 49 and y -20 to +20. Every line's two-digit number is printed in black, 6 cm tall (Oswald Bold), upright for a reader at the near edge, on two opposite white margins: eastings in the near margin (centred at x 9) and the far margin (x 53), northings in both side margins (centred at y +24.5 and -24.5), each centred on its line. A small north arrow sits in the far margin's right corner. Map markers: two weighted acetal cylinders, 25 mm across and 40 mm tall, 40 g, each with an 8 mm white dot centred on its top: red, standing on the table at (25, +33), and blue at (25, -33). Both arms start at the ready pose with their grippers open. One fixed layout, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Read from the markers' poses every control step; in a real trial, a top photo and a ruler, measuring on the map from the centre lines of the printed grid lines. A marker's position is the centre of its base, where its axis meets the map (the white dot on top marks it). A marker is placed when all hold: it stands upright (axis within 5 degrees of vertical); its base rests on the map, within 3 mm of the map surface (not held up, not on the other marker, not off the board); both grippers' TCPs are at least 6 cm from the middle of its axis; and it has moved slower than 1 cm/s for the last 1 s. Inside a grid square: the position lies within the square, at least 1.5 cm from each of its four grid lines (so the 25 mm base touches no line). Red passes: placed and inside square 3234, whose south-west corner is the crossing of easting 32 and northing 34 (x 37.5 to 44.5, y +1.5 to +8.5). Blue passes: placed with its position within 1.0 cm of (28.5, -16.5), the centre of the 100 m square that 346 332 names (6 tenths east of easting 34, 2 tenths north of northing 33), so the whole 100 m square counts. Blue in its square: placed inside square 3433 (x 27.5 to 34.5, y -11.5 to -18.5) but more than 1.0 cm from that point. Score: 1.0 once red and blue pass together for 1 s (the trial then ends). Otherwise, at the run limit, 0.5 if red passes, plus 0.5 if blue passes or 0.25 if blue is only in its square; this gives at most 0.75, so the possible scores are 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75 and 1.0. In a real trial, a trial in which the board moves more than 1 cm scores 0 (in simulation it is fixed). Every other case: a marker earns 0 if it is outside its target, held, lying down, still moving, on the other marker, off the board or off the table; a marker of the wrong colour counts for nothing; markers may be moved and set down again, and the path does not matter. Examples: doing nothing 0; reading northing first 0 (red lands in square 3432, blue at (42.5, -2.5)); red on the crossing of lines 32 and 34, or in the square south-west of it, earns 0 for red; blue in the centre of square 3433 earns 0.25; red right and blue 1.5 cm from its point 0.75; colours swapped 0.
reset_notes: Stand the two markers back beside the board. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, 240 Hz physics, 20 Hz control. The map is a flat texture on a fixed box; the markers are plain cylinders with convex-hull colliders. The grid numbers are printed about 20 times larger than on a paper map, so they can be read at the cameras' resolution. Real markers would be pins or magnets; these stand freely. Acetal on laminate friction 0.5 (0.4 sliding).
